companyRankingLists.itemDescription:
The oil and gas pipeline and transportation production company jumped 17 places on this year’s list as Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine created an energy shortage that boosted demand in the sector.

  • The company was the most profitable pipeline firm on this year’s Fortune 500, bringing in $5.5 billion in profits in 2022, up 18% from the year prior.

  • The company’s $58 billion in revenue represented a staggering 43% increase from 2021, as oil prices rose significantly in 2022.

  • In February 2022, one of the company’s affiliates acquired Navitas Midstream for $3.25 billion, marking an expansion into natural gas processing.

companyRankingLists.itemDescription: Houston-based Enterprise Products provides midstream energy services—think processing, transportation, and storage—of natural gas, natural gas liquids, crude oil, and refined petroleum products. In 2021, the company posted 50% year-over-year revenue growth, jumping 16 spots on the Fortune 500 list. In April 2022 Enterprise Products Operating, a subsidiary of the company, announced that it would work toward a carbon dioxide and sequestration solution for the Texas Gulf Coast, a potential tool for fighting CO2 emissions and climate change.

companyRankingLists.description: Global business is back. After limping through a worldwide financial crisis and economic slowdown, the 500 largest companies ranked by revenues shattered all sorts of performance records in 2013: They racked up combined revenues of $31.1 trillion, up 2.5% from 2012, and profits soared 27% to nearly $2 trillion. China’s 95 companies (up from 89 last year) posted $5.8 trillion in revenues. The U.S. has four fewer companies on the list than last year but remains (for now) the country leader, with 128 corporations on the list—including No. 1 Wal-Mart Stores—reporting $8.6 trillion in revenues.
